root_cause: VAL reconstruction scores are heavily right-skewed (skewness=19.94) AND uniformly < 1 (range [0.000247, 0.348751]). Because all values are already sub-1, log1p(x)=log(1+x) is numerically close to the identity there, so it barely reduces skew (19.94 -> 18.91) and would not meaningfully fix calibration. A raw log(score+eps) transform is the correct choice for sub-1 multiplicative-scale data: it reduces skew to 2.00 and yields a well-scaled Platt slope (a=2.97 vs raw a=25.03), improving average calibration (ECE 0.4816 -> 0.0237). However log-Platt introduces a NEW measured failure: overconfidence in the sparse high-score tail (gap=0.737 in the top probability bin), which is why isotonic regression and temperature scaling are compared in Part A rather than adopting log-Platt outright. On THIS leak-free split the historical catastrophic blowup (a~700) did not reproduce (raw Platt here: a=25.0, not saturated) — that specific failure was tied to the old leaky evaluation pipeline / old model, not an inherent property of Platt scaling itself.
